correctness.rationale: For each selected induced complete multipartite subgraph with selected size s and largest part occupancy L, longest ordinary path length is min(s,2(s-L)+1). A P_k-free set therefore has size <=k-1 or outside-dominant count q<=floor((k-2)/2). Count all sets by unique dominant part for s>=k; inclusion maximality forces either (k-1)-sets with each part <=ceil(k/2)-1 or an entire dominant part plus exactly t outside vertices, with V(G) alone in the no-k-path case. Derivation covers k=4, k=N, small parts, ties and even/odd bipartite k; the complement gives minimal covers. Inspected original verify.py adjacency DFS. Fresh direct ordinary-path search and maximal-set extraction agreed with every coefficient across 207 multipartite size/k instances on total order 4..8.

evidence: Published dissociation polynomial describes induced maximum-degree-one sets / P3-free sets; submitted explicitly restricts to k>=4.
Tu reports bipartite scalar k-path cover numbers, and Li–Zuo abstract offers exact values of ψ_k, not coefficientwise enumeration.

evidence: Occupancy lemma min(s,2q+1) is classical combinatorial input, not the full enumeration of maximal sets.
Bipartite odd k supports {2h,m+h-1} and even k one support, neither follows solely from a minimum cardinality.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Previous extremal values are consequences of the new maximal-set polynomial, but the implication does not reverse. Proof of all-formula requires novel maximality case split and coefficient enumeration.

evidence: Inclusion-minimal k-path covers are precisely complements of inclusion-maximal induced P_k-free sets, hence dual polynomial z^N M(z^-1).
Tu Theorems 37-38 list scalar minimum vertex-cover values, not all inclusion-minimal covers.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Mathematical object equals maximal independent sets in the hypergraph of all k-vertex paths; enumerator is not reducible to the minimum cover number alone.

originality.rationale: Prior minimum k-path vertex-cover formulas yield only extremal cardinality, not the complete polynomial of all feasible sets or inclusion-maximal sets. General dissociation polynomial handles k=3 and does not imply the new k>=4 classifications; prior longest-path occupancy lemma is explicitly credited. No prior all-complete-multipartite k-path transversal-size polynomial found in the checked primary survey and published records.

value.rationale: Path-transversal sets are natural graph deletion/hitting structures; knowing every inclusion-minimal solution and its cardinality distribution is a stronger mathematically motivated invariant than a minimum cover number. The sharp bipartite even/odd collapse, large gaps and asymptotic rarity of large maximal sets clarify a genuine structural phenomenon.
